findings.reason: §2's scope collapses from "perform every resolution" to "resolve the mount on the dry-run entry, reusing the owner," and the plan should cite resolve_project_repository (dispatch.py:249) at the dispatch.py:6586 call site as the mechanism to reuse, or the author will re-derive a parallel resolver.
findings.text: §2 says the dry run "does not resolve the plan and section against the worktree base ref" and that "every one of them is skipped today," but the dry-run CLI (reckon/cli.py:2052) already calls `plan_dispatch`, which already runs `require_plan_section_visible` (dispatch.py:5529) and `require_plan_reviewed` (dispatch.py:5536). The sole divergence from the real path is that `dispatch()` resolves the project mount via `resolve_project_repository` at dispatch.py:6586 and passes `repo=repo_root` (dispatch.py:6653), while the dry-run CLI passes the raw `--repo` option through unresolved (reckon/cli.py:2058), so `plan_dispatch`'s guard `if verdict.ok and repo is not None` (dispatch.py:5486) skips the whole authority block. The plan describes rebuilding machinery that exists instead of naming the one owner (`resolve_project_repository`, dispatch.py:249) whose invocation must be extended on the dry-run entry

findings.reason: the decision `member-repository-requirement` can be locked to "project alone" now from the schema, and §3's done-when narrows from an open investigation to asserting that a member resolves from the project alone and that the repository-requiring refusal is removed.
findings.text: §3 leaves the decision "is a roster member resolvable from the project alone, or does it require a repository?" open, saying "[t]he evidence for the decision is in the roster: if members can be registered against several repositories then the repository is genuinely needed." That evidence is already readable in the code: `register_member` (reckon/ledger.py:1746) stores only `id`, `harness`, `role`, `session_id` and session history — there is no repository field — and `members(project, root)` (reckon/ledger.py:1469) reads the roster from the project's own ledger, so a member is registered per-project and cannot belong to several repositories. The roster therefore already answers the plan's open decision (project-alone; the codex-b refusal naming `--repo` is the bug), yet the plan proposes to keep it unresolved and dispatch a test to discover it

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design edits the shared `plan_dispatch` in place (dispatch.py) and adds no new module, so there is no scaffolding of shallow wrappers to hide behind.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan's write path is the owning file `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` and its design reuses the shared resolution sequence rather than forking it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 asks the dry run to perform resolutions that the shared `plan_dispatch` already performs; the only actual gap is that the dry-run entry passes an unresolved `--repo` while the real entry resolves the project mount, so the design over-states the work and names no owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper is proposed; §2 makes the existing resolution path reachable rather than layering a second surface over it.
